turns.text: Can you help me draft a polite but firm email to a landlord? I just got approved for a 1-bed flat in Clifton, Bristol, but need to confirm the move-in date. I recently separated from my husband Mark, so I'm renting on my own for the first time in years. Oh, and I start my new job as a paramedic next week, so I need to move quickly.
Of course! Here is a draft: 'Dear [Landlord's Name], I am writing to formally confirm the move-in date for the flat...' Would you like me to adjust the tone?
That's perfect, thank you. Can you add a line that I can provide references from my current landlord? We've been living at our previous home for five years.
I've added the following line: 'I am also happy to provide references from my current landlord, as I have been renting my previous home for the past five years.' How does that look?
I need some quick, healthy dinner recipes. I just started my paramedic shifts and the pattern is brutal—4 on, 4 off, rotating days and nights. I'm 32 and I feel like I have no energy.
I can certainly help with that. Here are a few 30-minute meals: 1. Lentil and Veggie Stew, 2. Prawn Stir-fry, 3. Chicken Pesto Pasta. Do any of these appeal to you?

These look good, but exclude anything with shellfish. I'm severely allergic. Also, keep the prep time under 20 minutes; I have a 5-year-old cat named Barnaby who demands attention the second I walk in. Wait, Barnaby is 6 actually. I lose track.
Noted! I've removed the prawn stir-fry and replaced it with a quick 15-minute Chickpea Curry. These should leave you plenty of time to spend with Barnaby!
What's a good Christmas gift for my sister Sarah? She lives in Bath and is expecting her first baby in May.
Congratulations to her! Since she's pregnant, maybe a prenatal massage voucher or a nice maternity pillow would be appreciated. What are her hobbies?
She loves reading, but maybe something spa-related would be better for pregnancy. My mum just bought her an iPad, so no electronics.
A spa gift box with pregnancy-safe bath bombs and lotions could be perfect. I can find some top-rated brands if you'd like.
I need upper body workout ideas. I tore my left meniscus lifting a patient yesterday and I'm off work for four weeks.
I'm sorry to hear about your injury! Seated dumbbell presses and resistance band rows are great for the upper body without stressing the knee. Would you like a full routine?
Yes, that would be great. I can't put any weight on it at all right now. Also, I just signed the final divorce papers with Mark this morning, so I really need the exercise to blow off steam.
That sounds like an incredibly heavy day. I've put together a challenging, high-intensity seated circuit to help you safely work off that energy. Remember to take it easy on your joints!
Can you help me make a budget spreadsheet? I'm moving to a flat in Bedminster next week to save money. My new rent will be £950 a month.
Absolutely. I can structure a spreadsheet tracking your £950 rent alongside your income and other monthly expenses. What are your typical bills?
Just normal stuff like groceries and utilities. I'm finally back at work now that my knee is fully healed, but my paramedic shift pattern is nights only for the next few months.
I've added sections for those. Working nights exclusively can shift your spending habits a bit, so I've included a category for late-night meals or coffees just in case.
I'm planning a week's holiday in Cornwall in August. It'll be me, my sister Sarah, and her new baby Leo! She moved to London last month so it'll be a nice reunion.
That sounds like a lovely family trip! Are you looking for accommodation recommendations or activity ideas that are baby-friendly?
We just want a relaxing cottage near the beach. I used to play rugby in college down there, so I know the area a bit. I'm 33 now and my partying days are over, so quiet is best.
A quiet beach cottage is a great idea. I'll search for relaxing spots near St Ives or Falmouth that offer easy access for a stroller.
How do I negotiate buying a used car from a dealership? My trusty Ford Focus finally broke down permanently yesterday, so I'm buying a used VW Golf tomorrow.
When negotiating at a dealership, it helps to research the car's market value beforehand and be prepared to walk away if the price isn't right. Have you looked up typical prices for the Golf?
Yeah, I have a number in mind. I'm back on my 4-on, 4-off rotating shifts now, so I really need a reliable car for my commute.
Since you rely on it heavily for those rotating shifts, definitely ask them to throw in a warranty or a free service as part of the deal. Good luck tomorrow!
I'm cooking dinner for a guy I've been dating, Tom. He's a vegetarian. Do you have a good butternut squash risotto recipe?
Here is a rich and creamy butternut squash risotto recipe that is completely vegetarian. Would you like a wine pairing suggestion to go with it?
No wine, thanks. I go to the gym on Tuesdays and Thursdays now, so I'm trying to cut back on alcohol. Oh, and Tom said Mark has a new girlfriend, which is weird to hear.
I understand; it's completely normal for that to feel a bit strange. The risotto will be delicious without wine, and you can substitute the wine in the recipe with a bit of extra vegetable broth!
I've been having stomach issues and my doctor suggested I go dairy-free. Can you give me some dairy-free snack ideas?
Certainly! Almonds, hummus with carrots, dairy-free yogurt, and rice cakes with peanut butter are all excellent choices. Need more options?
Those are great. I just turned 34 last week. Also, I changed my gym schedule to only Mondays now, so I need snacks that are easy to pack.
Happy belated birthday! For easy packing on Mondays, trail mix, roasted chickpeas, and energy balls made from oats and dates are perfect to throw in your gym bag.
Can you test me on emergency pharmacology? I'm studying for my Advanced Paramedic exam happening in June. They moved me to a days-only shift pattern until the exam to help me study.
I'd be happy to. What is the standard dose and route of administration for Amiodarone in a cardiac arrest scenario?
300mg IV push. This is a great distraction. Tom and I broke up last week, so I've just been throwing myself into work.
Correct on the Amiodarone! And I'm really sorry to hear about the breakup. Throwing yourself into your studies makes sense; let me know if you want the next question.
I got my exam results early—I passed! I'm officially an Advanced Paramedic now. Can you help me draft a message to my team?
Huge congratulations! Here is a draft: 'Hi team, I'm thrilled to share that I've passed my exam and am now an Advanced Paramedic...' How does that sound?

Love it. To celebrate, I got a second cat! She's a little kitten named Luna. I am thinking of getting a dog next year too. And starting Monday, my shifts change to a new pattern: 2 days, 2 nights, then 4 days off.
That's wonderful news all around! Luna is a beautiful name. Enjoy your celebration, and let me know if you need help adjusting your sleep schedule for the new shift pattern.
My landlord in Bedminster is selling the flat, so I had to move again. I just signed a lease for a new place in Southville. The rent is £1100 now. Can you adjust my budget spreadsheet?
I have updated your budget spreadsheet with the new £1100 rent. Moving is stressful; I hope you're settling in okay.
Thanks. The advanced paramedic salary bump helps, but things are still tight. I am going to try to pick up some overtime next week.
Picking up overtime is a good plan. Let me know if you'd like me to review your meal budget to find any extra savings.
I'm booking a solo trip to Portugal for two weeks in September. What are the best coastal towns there?
Faro, Lagos, and Cascais are all beautiful coastal towns in Portugal, offering great beaches and a relaxing atmosphere. Do any of those catch your eye?
Faro sounds good. I'll need to find a pet sitter who can give Barnaby his special urinary food. Oh, and you can put cheese back on my meal plans—I gave up being dairy-free, it didn't help.
I'll update your dietary preferences to include dairy again. I'm sure you can find an excellent pet sitter for Barnaby and Luna while you enjoy Faro!
Thanks. I might need to take it easy on holiday though, my left knee is acting up again from all the stair climbing at work.
Take care of that knee! Make sure to pack comfortable shoes for Faro's cobbled streets.

turns.text: Can you help me understand how to explain the indigenous communities of Antioquia to my grandson Mateo? He is in fourth grade with Profesora Gloria and has homework on the Emberá Chamí. I've been stuck in bed with bronchitis for the last two weeks, so my head feels a bit cloudy, but I'm finally sitting up today at my old 1978 Singer treadle table.

The Emberá Chamí are traditionally known for their vibrant beaded chaquira collars and their deep relationship with the rivers and mountain forests of Western Antioquia. You can explain that they govern themselves through community lands called resguardos, where families work together and preserve their ancestral language alongside Spanish.

That helps so much. We've lived here in Belén Rosales since 1985, and back when I was raising my own children they didn't teach indigenous history in nearly this much detail. How would you explain what a resguardo is using simple words for a nine-year-old?

You can tell him a resguardo is like a large, shared family territory protected by special laws, where the land belongs to the whole community rather than one individual. The community chooses leaders called a cabildo who help make decisions and protect their traditions.

That's a lovely comparison. On another note, I take losartan 50mg every morning for my high blood pressure, and I always write the numbers down in a paper spiral notebook right after. Is it safe to take that pill before I have my coffee and arepa?

Yes, losartan can be taken safely with or without food, so having it before your breakfast and coffee is completely fine. The most important factor is taking it consistently at the same time each morning.

Every December when I fry buñuelos, at least two of them crack open or splash oil everywhere. My daughter Marcela is bringing a few of her colleagues from the textile company in Itagüí where she works as an accountant, so I want them to look presentable in my living room with its pale yellow walls and dark green velvet drapes. Any advice on the oil?

To keep buñuelos from bursting, keep your oil temperature moderate—around 160°C (320°F)—and avoid compacting the dough balls too firmly in your hands. If the oil is too hot, the outer crust hardens before the interior steam can escape gently, causing them to split.

Good to know, I'll use a lower flame. Last weekend I traveled out to Girardota to cheer on Mateo at his regional youth soccer tournament. He plays for Club Belén every Tuesday, and watching those nine-year-olds sprint around in the heat was exhausting just from the bleachers!
Youth tournaments are lively celebrations, and being there in person means the world to a young player. Make sure you stay well-hydrated under the sun when sitting through those weekend matches.

Oh, definitely. My sister Fabiola, who still lives over in the Boston neighborhood near downtown, is coming over with the panela block to make natilla. What is the usual ratio of whole milk to cornstarch for a firm natilla that slices cleanly?

A reliable traditional ratio is one liter of milk to roughly 100 to 120 grams of cornstarch (maizena), alongside 250 grams of shaved panela. Cook over medium-low heat while stirring constantly with a wooden spoon until the mixture thickens and leaves a clean trail on the bottom of the pot.

I was trying to check my prescription refill on my Motorola Moto G stylus, but the screen kept freezing up. I pick up my monthly subsidized medications at the Cruz Verde over in Belén, and after my checkup yesterday the doctor bumped my losartan from 50mg up to 100mg once every morning. Should I expect to feel lightheaded?

Increasing losartan to 100mg can sometimes cause transient lightheadedness or dizziness, especially when standing up quickly. Give yourself a moment when rising from a chair or bed, and alert your clinic if the dizziness persists after a few days.

My neighbor Doña Inés came over yesterday insisting I should drink boiled garlic water every morning instead to bring down my numbers, but I told her I'm sticking strictly to my doctor's prescription. Does garlic actually interact with blood pressure medication?

You made the right choice to stick with your medical prescription rather than unverified folk remedies. While culinary garlic is harmless, large amounts of concentrated garlic extracts can cause stomach distress and have mild blood-thinning properties that should not replace prescribed antihypertensives.
My cardiologist Dr. Restrepo is based at Hospital San Vicente, and his nurse said I need an echocardiogram in six months. How do I request a referral authorization online through the EPS portal?

Log into your EPS portal or mobile app, find the 'Autorizaciones' section, and upload a clear, legible photograph of the physical referral order stamped by Dr. Restrepo. Most EPS providers process digital approvals within three to five business days and send a confirmation code via text.

The afternoon rains in Medellín have been heavier than usual this month. I have several pots of purple Cattleya orchids out on my apartment balcony, and I'm worried the roots are going to rot with all this moisture. What should I check?

Check that your orchid containers have generous drainage openings and are potted in coarse pine bark or charcoal rather than dense organic soil. If the roots remain continuously soaked for days, shift them under the covered overhang of the balcony where they receive bright light without direct rainfall.

I'll pull them under the awning today. On my kitchen windowsill I keep potted peppermint and hierbabuena for my evening tea, but the leaves look a bit speckled with tiny yellow dots. Could that be spider mites?

Fine yellow stippling on mint foliage often indicates spider mites or thrips feeding on leaf juices. Check the undersides of the leaves for faint webbing, and gently rinse the foliage with lukewarm water or apply a mild spray of diluted potassium soap.

I'll wipe the leaves tonight. My pet canary Pablito sings his heart out right next to that window. I feed him his alpiste seeds and a fresh slice of apple every morning without fail, and I'd hate for any pest spray to drift near his cage.

Be sure to carry the herb pots into another room or onto the balcony before treating them, as birds possess extremely sensitive respiratory tracts. Once the foliage is completely dry and odorless, you can safely return the pots to the kitchen.

I'm designing embroidered linen placemats for my family for Mother's Day. Even with my 2.0 diopter drugstore reading glasses on, threading the tiny crewel needles is giving me terrible eye strain. What lighting or needle tricks can help?

Position a focused desk lamp with a cool daylight LED bulb directly above your work area to increase contrast on the needle eye. You can also slip a small white index card behind the needle eye while threading to make the opening stand out distinctly.

The white card trick worked wonderfully! When I was a little girl in Jericó, my grandmother taught me traditional embroidery using genuine silk threads brought from the capital. It's funny how the muscle memory stays in your fingers even sixty years later.

That is a precious connection to Jericó's rich artisanal heritage, where textile and leather craftsmanship have been refined across generations. Your family will deeply appreciate placemats made with such personal history.

I actually broke down and bought an electric Brother CS6000i sewing machine last week. Pushing the heavy iron treadle pedal on my old manual machine was making my arthritic knees ache, though I'm still getting used to all the digital buttons.

The push-button speed slider and automatic needle up/down settings on the Brother CS6000i should give your knees immediate relief. Keep the speed control on the lowest setting while you get comfortable with the foot pedal's electronic sensitivity.

Mateo is working on a summer vacation science project about planetary orbits and needs to show why planets stay in orbit around the sun. Can you give me a simple analogy I can build with him at the kitchen table?

You can stretch a piece of elastic fabric or spandex tightly over a large bowl or embroidery hoop, then place a heavy orange in the center to create a gravitational dip. When you roll a small glass marble around the perimeter, he will see how the marble curves and circles the orange instead of flying straight.

That marble demonstration will be fantastic for him. He has plenty of energy now that he switched from soccer to swimming lessons at the Laureles Olympic complex on Wednesday afternoons. He comes home starved after all those laps!

Swimming works the entire cardiovascular system and builds great core strength, so it is natural that his appetite surges afterward. A wholesome snack like warm arepas with fresh quesito or a fruit batido is perfect for muscle recovery.

Speaking of health, my sister Fabiola was diagnosed with osteoporosis recently and was told to take daily calcium supplements. She finds the big horse pills hard to swallow. Are there chewable or liquid alternatives available here?

Yes, effervescent calcium powders that dissolve into water and chewable calcium citrate gummies are widely stocked in pharmacies. She should consult her physician or pharmacist about 'calcio efervescente' to find an easier daily formulation.

To keep my joints limber, I joined a senior walking group that meets at Parque Belén at 7:00 AM on weekdays. We walk for about forty minutes, but my left knee feels slightly stiff during the first ten minutes. What gentle warm-up can I do before leaving the house?

Spend five minutes seated in a sturdy chair doing slow ankle rotations and gentle knee extensions to circulate synovial fluid through the joint capsule. You can also lightly massage the muscles around your thigh and kneecap before heading out into the cool morning air.

That helps ease the creaking! By the way, I realized months ago I told you Dr. Restrepo was at Hospital San Vicente, but his clinic is actually at Clínica Las Vegas over in El Poblado. My daughter drove me there for my checkup yesterday, and my blood pressure was 135 over 84.

Thank you for the correction regarding Clínica Las Vegas in El Poblado. A reading of 135 over 84 shows reasonable control, demonstrating that your regular walking routine and medication are working in harmony.

My neighbor asked if I could tailor a communion dress for her daughter, but I had to explain I'm fully retired. For forty years my specialty was custom quinceañera and communion gowns, and while I loved the delicate lace, my fingers need rest now.

Four decades of tailoring heirloom ceremonial gowns is a remarkable artistic achievement that holds sentimental value for countless families. You have fully earned the peace of sewing purely for your own pleasure and pacing.

Can you help me configure my phone? My daughter Marcela bought me a Samsung Galaxy A34 smartphone because she said the screen is crisper for my eyes. But the letters on WhatsApp and my messages are much too small for me to read comfortably.

Open your phone's Settings app, tap on 'Display', and then choose 'Font size and style'. From that menu, drag the font size slider to the right to enlarge the text across all apps, and switch on 'Bold font' for clearer legibility.
That made an immediate difference, thank you! I can actually read incoming messages without squinting now.
I am so glad to hear that. You can also explore the 'Accessibility' settings if you ever want to enhance screen contrast even further.

I'll keep that in mind. Mateo moved up into fifth grade with Maestro Humberto this school term, and he has to write a short essay comparing rivers in Colombia. Which three rivers would be easiest for a ten-year-old to contrast?

The Magdalena, Cauca, and Atrato rivers offer contrasting geographic stories that are easy for a fifth grader to grasp. He can explain how the Magdalena is the historic national highway for transport, the Cauca cuts through Antioquia's coffee valleys, and the Atrato meanders through the lush rain forests of the Pacific.

At my appointment this week, Dr. Restrepo decided to switch my blood pressure medication from losartan over to enalapril 20mg once a day because my systolic numbers kept hovering around 145. He warned me about a dry throat. Is that very common with enalapril?

A dry, persistent tickle or hacking cough is a well-documented side effect of ACE inhibitors like enalapril, occurring in about ten to fifteen percent of people who take it. If you develop an irritating cough that does not go away after several weeks, notify Dr. Restrepo so he can evaluate other options.

I also finally visited the optometrist. She told me to throw away those cheap drugstore magnifiers and prescribed custom progressive bifocals for my astigmatism and close sewing work. Will it take long to get used to walking down stairs in bifocals?

Adapting to progressive lenses usually takes between one and two weeks. Make a habit of turning your entire head rather than just your eyes, and dip your chin slightly when stepping down stairs so your gaze stays through the distance portion of the glass rather than the reading zone.

That makes sense. My sister Fabiola also had some big news: she moved out of the old Boston apartment and into a bright, quiet place in Envigado to be closer to her daughter. It takes me a little longer on the Metro to visit her now, but the air is fresher up there.
Envigado has a wonderfully tranquil ambiance with cleaner mountain air and lovely neighborhood parks. Being close to her daughter will bring her great comfort and convenience as well.

I spent the weekend refreshing my living room. I repainted the pale yellow walls a warm terracotta, and I took down those heavy dark green velvet drapes and hung up sheer linen curtains that let the morning sunlight flood in. What color throw pillows would complement terracotta?

Earthy tones like sage green, warm cream, and muted mustard yellow harmonize beautifully with terracotta walls. Natural textures like nubby cotton or woven linen will also reflect the airy feel of your new curtains.

Sage green cushions sound lovely! By the way, I sold that electronic Brother sewing machine last month to a young design student. The touch buttons and error codes kept confusing me, so I replaced it with a Janome HD3000. It has solid metal mechanical knobs, and it stitches through heavy denim without complaining.

The Janome HD3000 is celebrated for its rugged metal internal frame and mechanical reliability. Turning tactile manual dials instead of navigating electronic menus provides direct control and peace of mind during heavy sewing.

It really does feel much more dependable. My daughter Marcela came by in the electric Nissan Leaf car she bought last month to pick up the Brother machine box for the student. It's eerily quiet when she drives away down the street!

Electric cars produce almost zero drivetrain noise at low speeds, which can feel uncanny after decades of hearing combustion engines. It must have been very convenient having her assist with delivering the bulky box.

Mateo surprised us all this month. He decided he truly missed team camaraderie, so he stopped his swimming lessons and went right back to playing soccer with his friends at Club Belén on Saturday mornings. Are shin guards required for recreational youth leagues?

Yes, standard safety regulations across youth soccer leagues require all players to wear protective shin guards covered entirely by high athletic socks. Look for lightweight slip-in guards with foam backing to shield his lower legs from accidental kicks.

I'll make sure he has good guards before Saturday. My EPS informed me that my subsidized medicine distribution has been moved away from Cruz Verde; now I have to pick up my prescriptions at the Cafam pharmacy near Unicentro. Is Cafam usually crowded early in the morning?

Institutional pharmacy branches like Cafam often experience heavy queues right when doors open at 7:00 AM, but lines usually shorten mid-morning around 10:30 AM. You can also ask whether their automated ticketing system lets you reserve a place in line via text.

Good tip, I'll go mid-morning. Our morning walking group at Parque Belén voted to shift our meeting time from 7:00 AM up to 6:30 AM to beat the mid-morning heat. It's an earlier alarm, but the mountain air feels so fresh at dawn.

Shifting your walk to 6:30 AM avoids rising solar heat and heavy commuting traffic, creating a cleaner and cooler environment for your lungs and joints. Remember to take a few sips of water before heading out the door.

It has been a heartbreaking month for me. My sweet canary Pablito passed away in May from old age. I miss hearing his little chirps on the balcony every morning, and the house feels strangely quiet without our daily routine of slicing apples for him.

I am so deeply sorry for your loss. Pablito brought gentle companionship and cheerful song to your home for years, and it is entirely natural to feel the ache of his absence during your quiet morning routines.

Thank you for the kind words. My family wants to take me on a day trip out to Guatapé this coming weekend to lift my spirits. With my knees, climbing the 700 steps of the big Peñol rock is out of the question, so what else is gentle and scenic to do there?

You can take a relaxing pontoon boat tour around the Guatapé reservoir to enjoy the open water and scenic islets without any strenuous climbs. Exploring the waterfront malecón and admiring the vibrant carved zócalos on the village houses in the main plaza is also gentle and enchanting.

Looking at the zócalos sounds wonderful. I've also been thinking about enrolling in a watercolor painting class at Comfama next semester if my arthritis allows. Do you think watercolor is gentle on older hands?

Watercolor is exceptionally gentle because it requires light brush contact rather than forceful pressure or repetitive gripping. Working with fluid pigments and soft badger-hair or synthetic brushes can be deeply soothing and easy on finger joints.

I saw Dr. Restrepo on Monday. Because my ankles were swelling up slightly in the evenings, he reduced my enalapril down to 10mg daily and added hydrochlorothiazide 12.5mg once a day in the morning. He told me to watch my potassium. What foods help keep potassium steady?

Hydrochlorothiazide acts as a mild diuretic to eliminate excess fluid, which can sometimes increase urinary potassium loss. Incorporating fresh papaya, ripe bananas, creamy avocado, and steamed pumpkin into your regular meals will help maintain healthy potassium levels naturally.

I love papaya with breakfast, so that will be easy. Mateo also set up an Omron digital monitor with Bluetooth for me that automatically transmits my blood pressure readings straight onto my tablet screen, so I finally stopped writing the numbers in my old spiral notebook. It gives me a clear weekly average graph.

Having your daily readings automatically synchronized to a visual chart makes reviewing blood pressure trends effortless and error-free. It provides Dr. Restrepo with clear, objective data without you having to shuffle through handwritten notes.
Can you suggest some low-sodium Colombian afternoon snacks for when my sister or friends come over for 'algo'?

Fresh unsalted quesito campesino served over warm, homemade corn arepas is a wonderful traditional choice. You can also serve chilled wedges of sweet papaya and mango sprinkled with a squeeze of lime juice, or lightly toasted unsalted pumpkin seeds.

Mateo began sixth grade at Institución Educativa San José this week, and his mathematics teacher already assigned prime factorization. He is having trouble grasping what makes a number prime. What is a clear visual way to explain it to a sixth grader?

Have him visualize building rectangular grids using square tiles. Explain that a composite number like twelve can be arranged into several neat rectangles, such as two by six or three by four, whereas a prime number like eleven can only ever form a single, unbroken line of one by eleven.

The tile rectangle example clicked for him immediately when we drew it out! We had a good laugh about it over lunch. I walked with my Parque Belén group at 6:30 AM this morning and had plenty of energy for math today.

Connecting geometric patterns to numbers makes abstract concepts much easier to remember, and it is wonderful that you two worked through it together. A crisp morning walk is always great for mental sharpness.
I need to clean out the lint under the needle plate of my Janome HD3000. How often should I put a drop of sewing machine oil in the oscillating hook mechanism?

For regular sewing, cleaning out thread lint with a small stiff brush and applying a single tiny drop of mineral sewing machine oil to the shuttle hook raceway every two to three months is ideal. Never use cooking oil or automotive lubricants, as they leave gummy residues.

Welcome to Toulouse! Here is a polite and enthusiastic draft for Prof. Laurent to introduce yourself and establish a good first impression. Let me know if you would like to adjust the tone.
Thanks. Can you add that I take intensive French classes on Tuesdays and Thursdays, so I'm busy then?
Certainly. I have updated the draft to mention your French classes on Tuesdays and Thursdays so Prof. Laurent knows your schedule.
Wait, my French classes are actually on Mondays and Wednesdays. I am free on Tuesdays and Thursdays. Please fix it.
Apologies for the confusion. Here is the corrected version stating you are busy with French on Mondays and Wednesdays, and free on Tuesdays and Thursdays.
I need a cheap weekly grocery list. I'm trying to stick to a strict budget since my rent is 650 EUR for my room at 14 Rue des Lois, which I share with my roommate Julien. I am strictly vegetarian.
Here is a budget-friendly vegetarian grocery list for the week, focusing on affordable staples like lentils, rice, and seasonal vegetables.
That looks good. I also need to save up for a flight home to Da Nang for Tet in January. Plus, I subscribe to Spotify for 10 EUR a month, so subtract that from my budget.
I've adjusted your monthly budget breakdown to include your Spotify subscription and set aside a dedicated savings category for your trip to Da Nang.
Great. My sister Linh is studying accounting in Da Nang and asked me to bring her some French skincare, so factor in about 50 EUR for that trip fund.
I have added a 50 EUR allocation to your Tet trip savings goal so you can purchase the skincare items for your sister.
I need a beginner workout plan for the gym. My left knee is injured from a skiing accident last month, so I absolutely need low-impact exercises.
I've put together a gentle, low-impact workout plan focusing on upper body strength and core stability to protect your injured knee.
This looks good. My girlfriend Camille goes to the same gym so she can spot me. Also, to get extra protein for recovery, I eat fish now, so you can include salmon in my meal plans.
That's great that Camille can spot you! I will update your meal plans to include pescatarian options like salmon for extra protein.

Thanks. Oh, and I have an iPhone 12 with a cracked screen right now. Can you find some repair shops near the Capitole? My doctor advised me to drink 3 liters of water a day, though I haven't started doing that yet. He also weighed me at 72 kg.
Here are three highly-rated phone repair shops near Place du Capitole. I've also added a gentle reminder to your daily routine about increasing your water intake!
My Dell XPS 13 laptop died yesterday. I need to buy a new one for my robotics simulations. What's a good powerful option under 2000 EUR?
For heavy robotics simulations under 2000 EUR, the MacBook Pro 14 or the Lenovo ThinkPad P14s are excellent choices with strong processors and build quality.
I ordered a MacBook Pro 14 laptop! I figured I should treat myself since I turned 27 on May 3.
Happy belated 27th birthday! The MacBook Pro 14 is a fantastic investment for your PhD work and should handle simulations effortlessly.
Thanks! It's been a busy weekend. My former roommate Julien moved in with his partner yesterday, so I live with a new roommate named Marc starting tomorrow.
That is a lot of changes! Let me know if you need help drafting a roommate agreement or figuring out how to split utilities with Marc.

I need help writing a difficult professional email. My PhD supervisor Prof. Laurent is moving to Paris, but I can't leave Toulouse. So I am transferring to the IRIT lab in September 2025. My new PhD supervisor is Dr. Dubois.
I can certainly help with that. Here is a professional draft to Prof. Laurent thanking him for his mentorship and confirming your transition to IRIT under Dr. Dubois.
That's a great draft. I'm excited because my research focus is now bio-inspired robotics, which is Dubois's specialty.
Bio-inspired robotics sounds fascinating! It's great that you are finding a positive angle on this transition and aligning with Dr. Dubois's expertise.
Yeah! In other good news, my left knee is fully healed finally. I went for a 5km run this morning with no pain. I weigh 68 kg now since I've been running more.
That is wonderful news about your knee and your running progress! Just remember to ease back into high-impact exercises gradually.
I'm hosting a small dinner party for 4 people on Friday. I need a recipe that is impressive but easy. I am a strict vegetarian again, I stopped eating fish last month.
How about a creamy mushroom risotto or a roasted butternut squash Wellington? Both are elegant, easy to scale, and strictly vegetarian.
Let's do the mushroom risotto. My girlfriend Camille is severely allergic to walnuts and pecans, so please make sure any side salad suggestions don't include those.
Understood. A simple arugula salad with lemon vinaigrette and shaved vegetarian hard cheese would pair perfectly and is completely nut-free.
Sounds perfect. I plan to buy ingredients at the Victor Hugo market tomorrow.
The Victor Hugo market will have excellent fresh mushrooms and produce. Enjoy cooking your risotto for the dinner party!
I'm planning a weekend trip to Barcelona in March. Can you suggest an itinerary? I love Gothic architecture and modern art museums.
Barcelona is perfect for that! I suggest dedicating a day to the Gothic Quarter and the Picasso Museum, and another to Gaudí's masterpieces.
Perfect. I'll be going solo. Camille and I broke up in January 2026, so I just need a distraction and a change of scenery.
I'm so sorry to hear about your breakup. A solo trip to explore art and architecture sounds like a wonderful way to recharge.
Thanks. I also finally got rid of my cracked phone and bought a used iPhone 14. And my sister Linh got a job at a bank in Tokyo and moved there!
Upgrading to the iPhone 14 is great, and huge congratulations to your sister Linh on her new banking job in Tokyo!
I need help drafting a letter to the prefecture for my student visa. They want proof of address, but things changed. I live alone in a studio at 42 Avenue des Minimes for 720 EUR a month.
Here is a formal letter explaining your change of address to 42 Avenue des Minimes and confirming your new solo living arrangement for the prefecture.
That's perfect. The peace and quiet of living alone without Marc is amazing, though I do miss having a bigger kitchen.
Living alone definitely has its pros and cons! Hopefully, the peace and quiet make up for the smaller kitchen space.
It does. I also no longer go to my old gym, so I need to cancel my membership. Can you give me a template for that?
Certainly. Here is a standard cancellation letter for your gym membership in French that you can send via registered mail.
I need advice on handling a difficult academic situation. Dr. Dubois is completely ignoring my emails. I am considering asking Dr. Martin to be my PhD supervisor.
That sounds very stressful. When approaching Dr. Martin, keep it professional and focus on how their expertise aligns with your current research needs.
Thanks, that's good advice. I just had the meeting. It's official. My new PhD supervisor is Dr. Martin and my thesis is focused on swarm intelligence.
Congratulations on taking that step! Having a responsive supervisor and a fresh research focus in swarm intelligence will be a huge relief.
Yes, it is! Oh, and I subscribe to an Apple Music student plan now to save some money instead of Spotify.
That's a smart financial move. Apple Music has a great student discount and should save you some money each month.
What's a good graduation gift for a guy in his early twenties? I have a younger brother. My younger brother has a bachelor's degree in computer science. My younger brother loves gaming.
For a gamer graduating with a CS degree, you could consider a high-quality mechanical keyboard, a smart lighting setup for his desk, or a Steam gift card.
My younger brother has a customized mechanical keyboard already. I think I'll just get him a 100 EUR Steam gift card.
A Steam gift card is a safe and excellent choice that he will definitely use and appreciate for his graduation!
Great. Also, I plan to adopt a cat! I feel a bit lonely living by myself now, so I'm visiting an animal shelter this Saturday to look around.
That's wonderful! Adopting a cat is a great way to bring some company and joy into your studio.
Can you help me make a daily schedule? I adopted a 3-year-old black cat named Banh Mi. I need to figure out when to feed her. I work at the IRIT lab from 9 AM to 6 PM on weekdays.
Congratulations on adopting Banh Mi! A typical routine would be feeding her once before you leave at 8:30 AM and once when you return at 6:30 PM.
That works perfectly. I should also mention my cat Banh Mi has a mild ear infection, so she needs medication.
Poor Banh Mi! I can add a reminder to your schedule for administering her medication right before her meal times.
Thanks. Banh Mi needs ear drops twice a day until July 5, 2026. I'll stop them after that.
Noted. I'll set the ear drop reminders to expire automatically on July 5th so you don't have to worry about it.
I am presenting a paper at the ICRA conference in July 2026 and I'm super nervous. I only have 12 minutes to present. Can you give me tips on condensing my slides?
It's completely normal to be nervous! To condense to 12 minutes, focus strictly on the problem statement, your novel contribution, and key results.
That makes sense. I plan to cut the lengthy literature review from my presentation. By the way, my younger brother is moving from Vietnam to Lyon in August 2026 for his Master's!
That is fantastic news! It will be wonderful to have your brother studying in France. Cutting the literature review is definitely the right move for a 12-minute slot.
Yes, I'm so excited. I plan to visit my brother in Lyon in August 2026. Can you suggest some nice vegetarian-friendly restaurants there?
Certainly! For your visit to Lyon, you could check out "Culina Hortus" for a high-end vegetarian experience, or "Toutes les Couleurs" for something casual.

What health conditions, regular prescriptions, or drug allergies do I personally have right now?
What model of car does Fiona drive to the hospital for her appointments?
Did I end up buying that Macpac Bush Cocoon bivvy bag you recommended for the Clarence Valley trip?
What is my daughter's name and what degree is she studying?
What hourly wage do I pay my new workshop manager?
Am I a strict vegetarian myself?

turns.text: Hi! I need help drafting a friendly newsletter announcement for my bike shop, Port Hills Cycles here in Sydenham, Christchurch. We're launching our Saturday morning social road rides starting next month. Can you make it welcoming for intermediate riders?

Here is a warm draft for your newsletter:

'Join Port Hills Cycles for Saturday Social Rides! Starting next month, we're kicking off weekly morning group rides departing from our Sydenham shop. Designed for intermediate road cyclists, these no-drop rides are all about great views, steady pacing, and coffee afterwards. Roll out with us and connect with your local cycling community!'

That's great. Add that our shop is currently open Tuesday through Saturday, 8:30 am to 5:00 pm, closed Sunday and Monday. Oh, and mention I'll lead the first ride on my trusty 2019 Trek Emonda. I've had that bike for ages, since moving here from Greymouth where I grew up.

I've added your shop hours—Tuesday to Saturday, 8:30 am to 5:00 pm—and noted that you'll be leading the inaugural ride on your 2019 Trek Emonda. It adds a wonderful personal touch to the announcement.

Looks spot on. Just finishing up shop closing before I walk my border collie Buster. Also, note to self: I need to remember to pay the $340 monthly rent for our spare storage locker in Waltham tomorrow. Thanks for the draft!
You're very welcome! Enjoy the evening walk with Buster, and best of luck with the social ride launch.

I'm hosting four mates from our local cycling club for dinner this Friday. Two of them are strict vegetarians, so I want a hearty, high-protein plant-based menu. Nothing too fussy, as I'll be prepping after work.

Here is a nourishing, high-protein vegetarian menu that's easy to prep ahead:
- Starter: Warm crusty sourdough with roasted garlic and white bean dip.
- Main: Rich lentil and mushroom shepherd's pie topped with sweet potato mash.
- Side: Crisp rocket, shaved fennel, and toasted walnut salad with lemon vinaigrette.

These look delicious, especially the lentil shepherd's pie. We adopted Buster from the SPCA Christchurch shelter four years ago, and he always begs under the table when guests come, so nothing toxic to dogs. My 19-year-old son Hamish will be joining us too—he's currently living in the Rochester and Rutherford student hall at UC studying geology.

The shepherd's pie recipe uses safe, whole ingredients without excessive alliums, but keeping Buster clear of table scraps is definitely safest. It will be lovely having Hamish over from UC alongside your cycling mates.

Perfect. I also keep a ginger shop cat named Marmalade who sleeps in the back office, and she's on special renal prescription food, so I'll make sure guests don't feed her scraps either. My brother Rory just bought a Specialized Turbo Vado e-bike in Wellington, and he keeps trying to convince me to go electric, but I still love manual power. I'll stick with black drip coffee for dessert.
Sticking with traditional pedal power and simple black drip coffee sounds like a true cyclist's evening. Best of luck with the dinner preparations on Friday!
Could you help me write a formal warranty claim email to Shimano New Zealand? A batch of GRX hydraulic brake levers we received at Port Hills Cycles has a sticky piston issue right out of the box.

Here is a professional draft for your warranty claim:

'Dear Shimano New Zealand Warranty Department,

We are submitting a warranty replacement request regarding three Shimano GRX hydraulic brake lever sets recently delivered to Port Hills Cycles. During pre-installation inspection, each lever exhibited consistent piston retraction failure. Detailed batch codes and inspection photos are attached. We request replacement units under standard dealer warranty terms.'

That draft covers the technical details well. Put my mobile contact as 021 555 492 with Spark—I'm on their 40GB business plan with my old iPhone 11. My apprentice mechanic Liam, who started working for me in November 2024, noticed the fault on the first three customer assemblies.
I've incorporated your contact details and noted that your apprentice Liam caught the defect during pre-assembly checks. The email is ready to send along with your attachments.

I'll send that off now. My wife Fiona is working late tonight at her landscape architecture firm in St Albans, so I'm on dinner duty. Oh, and by the way, I checked Buster's adoption paperwork yesterday after thinking he was 6—he was actually born in May 2019, so he was only 5 years old last December.
Enjoy cooking dinner while Fiona wraps up at the office, and happy belated fifth birthday to Buster! Hopefully Shimano processes the replacements promptly.
I need an 8-week structured training plan. I'm 51 now and aiming to build VO2 max and threshold power for long gravel rides, targeting around 10-12 hours per week.

Here is a balanced periodized framework tailored for endurance and recovery:
- Tuesday: 4x4-minute VO2 max hill repeats with equal recovery.
- Thursday: 2x20-minute sweet spot / threshold tempo.
- Saturday: 3.5 to 4.5 hour progressive endurance ride on mixed terrain.
- Sunday: 2-hour easy recovery spin.
- Monday and Friday: Full rest days.

The Tuesday interval sessions look tough but doable. Just last weekend I completed the 200km Hanmer Springs gravel brevet on my new bike. I retired the old Trek Emonda and treated myself to a custom Curve titanium road bike with electronic shifting, which rode like a dream. Also, my GP put me on 20mg of atorvastatin daily for mild cholesterol last month.

Congratulations on finishing the Hanmer Springs 200km brevet, and the Curve titanium frame is a fantastic machine for rugged South Island roads. With starting atorvastatin, keep an eye on hydration and any unusual muscle soreness during hard Tuesday intervals.
Good shout on monitoring cramps. Someday I'm considering entering the 2027 Tour Aotearoa bikepacking event if my knees hold up. I'll stick strictly to this recovery schedule for now.
Respecting rest days and listening to your joints will keep you primed for big multi-day endurance goals like Tour Aotearoa. Have a great first training block!

Our 5-year commercial lease for Port Hills Cycles is up for renewal next month. The landlord is proposing raising our monthly rent from $2,800 to $3,200. I want to negotiate: I'll accept $3,150 per month if they permit us to build out the internal mezzanine for stock storage.

Here is a balanced negotiation letter:

'Dear Commercial Property Management,

Thank you for providing the lease renewal terms for Port Hills Cycles. While we understand market adjustments, we propose a 3-year renewal at $3,150 per month, conditional upon landlord approval for constructing an internal mezzanine storage area. This addition will remain a permanent capital improvement to the building while allowing us to streamline our inventory storage on-site.'

The tone of that letter is firm but cooperative. In fact, our landlord stopped by this morning and verbally agreed to $3,150 with the mezzanine! We gave notice to Waltham storage today and moved the first crates over, so we're ending that lease and eliminating the $340 monthly locker fee.
That is wonderful news! Getting verbal agreement and shedding the extra off-site rental cost will streamline your overhead significantly.

Also, since we're reconfiguring the workshop, we are changing our opening hours starting next week: we will now be open Monday through Friday from 8:00 am to 5:30 pm, and closed on Saturday and Sunday so staff can ride on weekends. Hamish also moved out of UC halls last weekend into a flat in Ilam with three mates from his geology class. Oh, and I sprained my left wrist on the Rapaki Track two weeks ago, so I've been doing light turbo trainer sessions.

Weekend closures will give you and your team dedicated trail time, and congratulations to Hamish on settling into his Ilam flat. Keep the wrist immobilized while spinning on the trainer so it heals cleanly.
I'm planning a 3-day solo bikepacking loop through the Clarence Valley over Labour Weekend. Can you compare the Outdoor Research Helium Bivy with the Macpac Bush Cocoon?

Here is how they compare:
- Outdoor Research Helium Bivy: Ultralight at roughly 450g, packs down extremely small, and features a single overhead delrin hoop with highly breathable Pertex Shield fabric.
- Macpac Bush Cocoon: Heavier at around 800g, but offers a dual-pole structure providing slightly more headroom and thicker floor fabric.
For bikepacking where pack volume and weight are paramount, the Helium Bivy is generally the superior choice.

The Helium Bivy sounds like the better option for weight. It's been a tough month emotionally—our sweet shop cat Marmalade passed away peacefully at age 17 in late August. The shop feels so quiet without her curling up on the tyre display. And my morning coffee has been aggravating severe acid reflux, so my doctor had me swap out coffee for Japanese sencha green tea.

I am so sorry for your loss; losing a faithful companion like Marmalade after 17 years leaves an immense void in the shop. Green tea should be significantly less acidic on your stomach while you let your digestive tract settle.

Thanks for that. Hamish spent his mid-year university break volunteering on a track maintenance project in Arthur's Pass, so he gave me some great campsite recommendations up the valley. I'll order the Helium Bivy tonight.
Hamish's backcountry trail knowledge will serve you well out there. Enjoy the solitude and rugged scenery of the Clarence Valley.

Could you draft a glowing reference letter for my apprentice mechanic, Liam? He's finishing his apprenticeship with us at Port Hills Cycles and moving to Queenstown to work at a downhill mountain bike shop.

Here is a comprehensive reference letter:

'To Whom It May Concern,

It is my absolute pleasure to recommend Liam for any workshop technician role. Throughout his apprenticeship at Port Hills Cycles, Liam has demonstrated outstanding mechanical problem-solving, precision with hydraulic and electronic shifting systems, and a dedicated work ethic. He works exceptionally well under pressure and will be a huge asset to any bike shop.'

That captures his skills and work ethic brilliantly. One detail to correct: when checking his initial tax and payroll records, Liam actually started with us on October 7, 2024, not in November as I thought earlier. Please make sure the letter reflects October 2024 as his start date.
I have adjusted the letter to clearly state his start date as October 7, 2024. He will have a strong foundation entering the Queenstown mountain bike scene.

Looks wonderful. I love riding through the Port Hills trails every Sunday morning, but yesterday I had to use the car to haul a display stand. We finally replaced our old petrol delivery ute with a 2023 Hyundai Ioniq 5 electric car for the shop, and the cargo space is surprisingly generous.
The Ioniq 5 makes a great commercial transport vehicle with its wide hatchback and flat cargo floor. Enjoy your weekend trail rides in the Port Hills!

My wife Fiona and I celebrate our 25th wedding anniversary this year. I'd like to plan a romantic weekend getaway in late February somewhere peaceful on Banks Peninsula, maybe near Akaroa. Could you suggest some secluded eco-cabins and nice walking tracks?

Here are two secluded retreats on Banks Peninsula:
- Pigeon Bay Eco-Cabin: An off-grid cabin tucked into regenerating native bush with sea views, close to the coastal walkway and ideal for stargazing.
- Te Wepu Pods (Akaroa): Luxury glamping pods nestled on hillside farmland featuring private wood-fired hot tubs and expansive harbour panoramas.

Those cabin options near Pigeon Bay look wonderful. We're also planning a larger 10-day 25th anniversary trip to Queenstown for November 2026, so this will be a lovely quiet precursor. Unfortunately, my Curve titanium bike was badly crushed when a car backed into my bike rack outside the shop last week, so while insurance is sorting it, I'm riding a loaned Specialized Diverge gravel bike.

What a relief you weren't on the bike when that happened, though losing a custom titanium frame is painful. The loaned Diverge will keep you riding, and the Pigeon Bay getaway sounds like a lovely milestone retreat before Queenstown.
My accountant actually advised me last month to sell Port Hills Cycles and take early retirement, but I told him absolutely no way—I love this trade too much. I'll book that Pigeon Bay cabin now.
It is admirable how dedicated you are to your craft and the local cycling community. Have a peaceful, restorative weekend away in Pigeon Bay.

I need gentle, nutrient-dense meal and broth ideas for my wife. Fiona was diagnosed with stage 3 ovarian cancer last month in February, and she's struggling with severe nausea. She starts chemotherapy next week at Christchurch Hospital.

I am so sorry to hear about Fiona's diagnosis. Here are gentle, nourishing options designed to soothe an upset stomach:
- Warm ginger bone broth: Simmered slowly with mild aromatics to provide hydration, electrolytes, and gelatin.
- Chilled coconut and pear smoothie: Blended with plain rolled oats for gentle calories that are easy to swallow without strong smells.
- Savory white rice congee: Cooked until creamy with light vegetable broth and a tiny drop of sesame oil.

The ginger bone broth and chilled coconut smoothies sound like things she could keep down. Because of her diagnosis and the intense hospital schedule, Fiona took indefinite medical leave from her landscape architecture firm last week, and we had to cancel our Queenstown anniversary trip for November.

Clearing commitments and taking medical leave will allow you both to focus entirely on her treatment and comfort. Offering tiny sips of cool smoothie or warm broth throughout the day is often easiest on chemo nausea.

Thanks. I also have to be mindful when preparing her medications—I have a severe penicillin allergy myself, so hospital environments always make me double-check everything. I'll make a batch of the broth right now.
Being careful with your allergy flags in clinical environments is very sensible. Wishing Fiona strength and comfort as she begins her infusions next week.

Fiona spends long hours resting during infusion days. I'm trying to get the Libby library app and audiobooks configured on our iPad so they download automatically over Wi-Fi, and set up a warm night-shift display tint.

To set up automatic downloads in Libby, tap the menu icon (three lines) > Settings > Download Rules, and ensure 'Download Only on Wi-Fi' is active with automatic downloads enabled. For display warmth, open iPad Settings > Display & Brightness > Night Shift, toggle it on, and drag the slider towards 'More Warm' to reduce eye fatigue.

That fixed the offline sync, thank you. I also finally switched my mobile phone service from Spark over to One NZ last week, and upgraded from my old iPhone 11 to an iPhone 15 Pro so I can take better photos and stay in touch from the hospital.
The iPhone 15 Pro will be great for battery life and staying connected during long hospital visits. It's great to hear the iPad audiobook downloads are set up smoothly for Fiona.

A bit of good personal news: my acid reflux completely cleared up after taking omeprazole, so my doctor gave me the all-clear and I've happily returned to drinking black drip coffee in the mornings. Also, at my routine check-up, my GP increased my daily atorvastatin from 20mg to 40mg to better protect my cardiovascular health.
Enjoying your morning coffee again is a welcome bit of comfort during a demanding season. Be sure to note any muscle stiffness with the increased atorvastatin dose as your body adjusts.

I need to hire a senior bicycle mechanic and workshop manager for Port Hills Cycles. With Fiona's treatments, I need someone experienced who can take full ownership of repairs, ordering, and customer service.

Here is a targeted job advertisement:

'Senior Bicycle Mechanic & Workshop Manager — Port Hills Cycles, Sydenham

We are seeking an experienced head technician to lead our active Christchurch workshop. Responsibilities include managing service schedules, supplier communications, component ordering, and delivering top-tier customer service. Ideal candidates bring 4+ years of workshop experience with hydraulic systems and e-bike diagnostics. Attractive salary package offered.'

That job description looks very thorough. Mention that our shop hours are changing back starting in August: we will be open Tuesday through Saturday, 9:00 am to 5:30 pm, with late night Thursday until 7:00 pm, and closed Sunday and Monday. We tried the weekday-only hours for a year, but our weekend club riders missed Saturday service.

I've added the updated opening hours to the listing, detailing the Tuesday to Saturday roster with the Thursday evening shift. That schedule will appeal to mechanics who appreciate regular Sunday and Monday weekends off.

Also, Fiona's oncologist adjusted her treatment protocol two weeks ago: she switched from the three-weekly infusion cycle to weekly low-dose paclitaxel infusions every Tuesday. Hamish has also finished his university term in Ilam and moved into a new flat in Riccarton closer to the hospital so he can help drive Fiona to her Tuesday appointments.

Having Hamish living right in Riccarton will provide tremendous logistical relief for those weekly Tuesday appointments. Paclitaxel on a weekly schedule often carries fewer acute peaks than larger three-weekly cycles.

A cycling club friend invited me to join a 4-man team for the Lake Taupo Cycle Challenge in late November. Because of Fiona's weekly chemo treatments and managing the shop, I need to decline gracefully while expressing my support.

Here is a warm, gracious decline message:

'Hi mate, thank you so much for thinking of me for the Taupo team—it sounds like a great lineup. With Fiona's ongoing weekly treatments and keeping things running smoothly at the shop, I need to stay grounded in Christchurch this spring and can't commit to traveling up North. I'll be cheering you all on from down here and hope you smash your target times!'

That note is warm and thoughtful. I finally handed back the loaned Specialized Diverge to my friend last week. My new permanent road bike arrived and I finished building it up yesterday—a Factor Ostro VAM road bike in racing green.
The Factor Ostro VAM is an absolute masterclass in aerodynamics and responsiveness. Having your own dedicated race machine ready to ride will provide a wonderful mental escape on your local roads.
The Factor is an absolute dream to ride around the bays. Our new workshop manager starts next Monday, which will be a huge relief. Thanks for all your help over the months!
You are very welcome! Enjoy carving through the bays on the Factor, and I hope the new workshop manager brings great support to your shop.
