turns.text: I need a workout plan. I'm 58 and work full-time as a marine mechanic, so my back is always shot from bending over outboard motors all day long in the shop. Plus I've got high blood pressure so nothing too crazy, I can't be doing crossfit or anything that's going to make my heart explode out of my chest.
Focusing on core and mobility is a great idea. We can start with gentle stretches and low-impact exercises.

Oh and I'm a single parent to three children, though they're mostly grown now. My two oldest children have moved out and my youngest child is 17 years old. Time is tight since I have irregular gig income and never know when a job is going to take four hours longer than I quoted. Can we do something like 20 minutes a day just to keep me limber?
20 minutes a day is absolutely enough to see benefits. I'll design a short, efficient routine.

Perfect. I take 10mg of Lisinopril in the morning, does that affect when I should work out? I read somewhere that blood pressure meds can make you dizzy if you jump around too much right after taking them, but I don't really know how true that is for this specific one.
Usually it is fine to exercise while on Lisinopril, but it is always best to double-check with your doctor.

Whatever, I'll just do it before I even have my first cup of coffee so I don't have time to talk myself out of it. Give me a schedule that I can stick to during the week, maybe leaving the weekends free since that's when I usually try to catch up on sleep or bigger projects.
Here is a 20-minute mobility and core schedule you can do Monday, Wednesday, and Friday before your coffee.

What's a good app to learn Canadian French? I've got a buddy who keeps talking about how we should take a trip up there and actually try to speak to the locals instead of just pointing at menus, but I don't know where to start without feeling like an idiot.
Duolingo and Babbel both offer excellent French courses, though you may need to learn standard French and adapt to the Canadian accent and vocabulary later.

I'm making an account on Babbel right now. My Babbel username is boatwrench58. I really need something to keep my hands and mind busy because I am quitting smoking. I'm on day three and the cravings are so bad I honestly want to murder a wrench right now just to let out some of this nervous energy.
Congratulations on making the decision to quit smoking! It is tough, but keeping your hands and mind busy with a new language is a great strategy.

Thanks. My friend Dave is learning French with me, so we're competing to see who can get through the lessons faster. He's incredibly competitive and it gets on my nerves. How do you say "I am going to crush you" in French so I can send him a voice note?
You can say "Je vais t'écraser" to tell him you're going to crush him.

He's going to absolutely hate that, which is excellent news for me. What about "you are slower than a turtle"? I want to have a few insults lined up for when he inevitably starts bragging about finishing a module before I do. The more sarcastic the better.
That would be "Tu es plus lent qu'une tortue."

I'm planning a fishing trip to Ontario for September. We're hoping to catch some walleye, but honestly, I don't know the first thing about crossing the border with all our gear. What kind of paperwork do I actually need to have ready so they don't turn my truck around at customs?
You will need a valid passport to cross the border, and an Ontario fishing license if you plan to fish.

Good to know. I am a US citizen, but I am looking into getting dual Canadian citizenship through my grandfather. He was born in Manitoba, so apparently I qualify, but we'll see how long the paperwork actually takes to process. In the meantime, the US passport will have to do.
That's an exciting process! Getting citizenship by descent can take several months to over a year, so a US passport will be best for this September trip.

Yeah, it's a process. Now I just gotta figure out what to do with my pets while I'm gone. I have an old beagle named Barnaby, and he absolutely hates kennels. He just howls the entire time and it breaks my heart, so I need to find another solution for him.
You might want to look into hiring a pet sitter who can stay at your house, so Barnaby can remain in his comfortable environment.

I'll ask my neighbor if she can watch him, she likes him anyway. By the way, my doctor increased my Lisinopril dose to 20mg because apparently quitting smoking didn't magically fix my blood pressure like I hoped it would. It's incredibly frustrating when you try to do the right thing and your body still complains.
I'm sorry to hear that, but managing it closely with your doctor is the best approach.

It is what it is, I guess. Are there any restrictions on bringing fishing gear across the border? I've got a bunch of custom lures and a couple of expensive rods, and I don't want any hassle from the border agents trying to claim I'm importing goods to sell or something.
Generally there are no restrictions on standard fishing rods and tackle, but live bait often faces strict import rules.

My sleep is an absolute disaster right now. I'm tossing and turning for hours. Help me build a wind-down routine that doesn't involve some ridiculous ten-step meditation process. I just need practical things I can do to tell my brain to shut off after a long day in the shop.
A good wind-down routine can work wonders. Try turning off screens an hour before bed, reading a book, and drinking some herbal tea.

Look, I have started smoking again. The stress of irregular income got to me when a big boat repair fell through. So "drink herbal tea" isn't going to cut it when I'm ripping heaters at 2 AM in the garage because I'm worried about paying the bills. I need realistic advice here.
Setbacks happen, and stress management is difficult. Try to separate your smoking environment from your sleep environment, and perhaps take a hot shower right before getting into bed.

Fine, I guess I have to try something different. I have a recurring physical therapy appointment for my shoulder on Tuesdays at 4 PM. Maybe I should do something relaxing right after that to kind of trick myself into starting the evening right instead of going straight back to work.
That's a great idea. Using that appointment as a transition into a more relaxed evening could help signal to your body that the workday is done.

Yeah, maybe a shower would help. What kind of stretches are good for shoulders? The physical therapist gave me a sheet of paper but I completely lost it somewhere in my truck, and I know I need to be doing something at home so it doesn't stiffen up again overnight.
Pendulum swings and wall crawls are excellent, gentle stretches to keep your shoulders mobile.

Draft an email to my landlord. My landlord's name is Mr. Henderson. He's a decent guy but very particular about everything being in writing. I need to talk to him about the space I'm renting, but I always get too casual when I write these things myself.

Dear Mr. Henderson,

I hope this email finds you well. I am writing to discuss my current lease...

Make it sound professional but remind him that I fix his outboard motor for free twice a year. I rent garage unit 4A right now, and it's getting way too cramped with the tools and the projects I've got going on. I can barely turn around in there without hitting something.

Dear Mr. Henderson,

I hope you're doing well and that the outboard motor is still running smoothly since I last serviced it. I am writing regarding my lease for garage unit 4A...

Good. Add that I officially rent garage unit 4B as of yesterday, and I removed the wall between garage units 4A and 4B to make a double-wide shop like we discussed. My friends Dave and Steve helped me tear down a wall this weekend. It took us like fourteen hours straight because Dave kept taking smoke breaks, but it's done. I'm hoping having all this extra space means I can take on bigger boat motors and stabilize my income a bit.

Dear Mr. Henderson,

I hope the outboard motor is still running smoothly. I am writing to confirm that, as discussed, I have officially taken over the lease for garage unit 4B as of yesterday. Additionally, my friends and I completed the removal of the wall between units 4A and 4B this weekend to create the double-wide shop space.

Thank you for working with me on this expansion.

I also adopted a stray cat named Socks. She just wandered into the shop one day and refused to leave, so she's mine now. My dog Barnaby is terrified of my new cat Socks, which is pathetic for a beagle, but that's just how it is. They'll figure it out eventually.
Congratulations on adopting Socks! It might take Barnaby a little while to get used to his new feline sibling. Do you want me to add anything about the cat to the email to your landlord?

No, he doesn't care about pets in the garage as long as they don't cause damage, so don't even mention the animals. Just send me the final text of the email so I can copy and paste it into my email client. I want to get this sent off today.

Here is the final text:

Dear Mr. Henderson,

I hope the outboard motor is still running smoothly. I am writing to confirm that, as discussed, I have officially taken over the lease for garage unit 4B as of yesterday. Additionally, I completed the removal of the wall between units 4A and 4B this weekend to create the double-wide shop space.

Thank you for working with me on this expansion.

Thanks for the help. Honestly, writing professional emails is the absolute worst part of running your own gig, so having you draft it takes a ton of the stress off my plate. I'll shoot this over to him right now.
You're very welcome! Let me know if you need help with anything else.

How do I stop my Android phone from backing up photos over cellular? I just got a notification that I've blown through my data cap for the month, and it's because my phone decided to upload three gigabytes of blurry engine part photos while I wasn't connected to the wifi.
To stop cellular backups on Android, open the Google Photos app, tap your profile picture, go to settings, select 'Backup', and turn off data usage for photo backups.

Got it. I had to change it because my Babbel username is minnesotaboats now, I got locked out of the old one and took a ton of screenshots trying to send proof to customer support to fix it. So annoying having my gallery filled with useless pictures of error screens.
Getting locked out of accounts is incredibly frustrating, especially when it clutters up your photo gallery with screenshots.

Yeah, exactly. By the way, I bought an old diesel F-250 for cheap and I am converting my F-250 to run on straight vegetable oil. I smell like french fries all day long, but given gas prices right now, I figure it's going to pay for itself by the end of the year.
That's a very unique and resourceful project! The french fry smell is a classic side effect of vegetable oil conversions.

It's definitely saving me money, which is a relief. Good thing, too, since my Lisinopril dose is now 40mg. Between the cost of the meds and the constant doctors visits, getting old is an absolute scam. I highly recommend staying young if you can manage it.
It can certainly feel that way sometimes. Make sure to get enough rest while working on the truck.

Always trying to rest, but it's tough. Is there a way to batch delete photos on Android? I really don't want to tap individually on all two hundred of those account recovery screenshots, there has to be a faster way to just wipe out a whole week's worth of pictures at once.
Yes, in Google Photos you can long-press on one photo, then drag your finger across others, or select entire dates to delete them in batches.

I need to update my workout routine. My shoulder is actually feeling a lot better from the physical therapy, but now my knees are starting to hurt when I do any kind of impact stuff. I swear, it's always one joint or another complaining these days. What can I do?
If your knees are bothering you, it's best to switch to low-impact exercises like swimming, cycling, or using an elliptical machine.

Okay, swimming maybe. The community center has a pool I can use. Oh, and I have quit smoking again. For real this time. Threw out all the ashtrays, threw out my secret stash in the toolbox. I am completely done with it. It was making me feel like garbage.
That's a huge step! Throwing out the ashtrays shows real commitment. Swimming will also be great for your lungs as they recover.

Yeah, it feels like a big step. But my dog Barnaby passed away last week. Old age finally caught up to him. So the house is real quiet and empty now. Socks keeps looking for him under the couch, which is breaking my heart. Just a rough couple of weeks.
I am so sorry for your loss. Losing a long-time companion like Barnaby is incredibly hard, and it's completely normal for Socks to be confused too.

Thanks. I'm just trying to focus on work to keep my mind off it. I removed the vegetable oil system from my F-250 because it kept clogging the fuel lines in the cold. I converted my F-250 to run on standard biodiesel instead. Much cleaner and a lot less hassle.
That sounds like a smart move. Biodiesel should give you much fewer maintenance headaches while still being a bit greener.

Yeah, the biodiesel is just way more reliable. Can you give me a 3-day swimming routine? Something that won't totally exhaust me, since I still have to stand on my feet for eight hours a day working on boats. Just enough to get my heart rate up a bit.
Day 1: 10 minutes warm-up, 15 minutes of freestyle. Day 2: 10 minutes warm-up, kickboard drills. Day 3: alternating fast and slow laps.

I want to start volunteering my time. How do I approach the local maritime museum about helping restore their old engines? They have all these beautiful antique boat motors that look like they haven't been maintained in decades, and I know I could get them running again if they let me.
The best approach is to find the contact info for their volunteer coordinator on their website and send a polite email detailing your professional mechanic experience.

I'll definitely do that. My physical therapy appointment moved to Thursdays at 3 PM, so I have Tuesdays free now to volunteer. It'll be nice to use my skills for something fun instead of just grinding away at gig work all the time just to pay the electric bill.
That opens up your schedule nicely! Having a dedicated free day will make it much easier to commit to a volunteer role.

Yeah, it should be good. Unfortunately, my friend Dave moved to Florida, the absolute traitor. He couldn't handle the winters anymore. Only my friend Steve helps me with heavy lifting at the shop now, which means things take twice as long because Steve has a bad back himself.
It's always tough when a good friend moves away. It's great that Steve is still around to help with the heavy lifting, though.

Thanks for the advice, I'll reach out to them today. What should the subject line of the email be? I want it to sound professional enough that they actually open it, but not so stiff that it sounds like I'm applying for a corporate desk job or something.
A good subject line would be "Volunteer Inquiry: Experienced Marine Mechanic for Engine Restoration."

Remember my landlord Mr. Henderson? I need another email drafted to him. He's still being a stickler for having absolutely everything documented in writing, and I really don't want to mess this up and get on his bad side since he's been pretty lenient with me in the past.
I can help with that. What is the situation this time?

I lost the lease on garage unit 4B. I just couldn't afford both units anymore with the way things are going. I need to put the drywall back up between garage units 4A and 4B by the end of the month. Ask him for a one-week extension on the wall rebuild.

Dear Mr. Henderson,

I am writing regarding the return of unit 4B. I am currently working on reinstalling the drywall between units 4A and 4B, but I would like to request a one-week extension to ensure the job is done properly.

Thanks. It really sucks having to shrink the shop back down, but gig work completely dried up this summer for some reason. At least my youngest child is going to college soon, so that's one less mouth to feed at home, even if the tuition is going to be brutal.
I'm sorry to hear work has been slow. Having your youngest head off to college is a huge milestone, though!

Make the tone of the email a bit more apologetic. I hate asking for extensions, especially when he's already being cool about letting me drop the second lease without a huge penalty. I just need a few more days to get the drywall mud to set right.

Dear Mr. Henderson,

I sincerely apologize for the delay, but I would be very grateful for a one-week extension on reinstalling the drywall between units 4A and 4B to make sure the work meets your standards.

Just wanted to share some good news. I am volunteering as an engine restorer at the local maritime museum. They actually brought me on! It's so cool getting to work on these old 1920s brass engines. It's completely different from the modern stuff I usually have to fix.
Congratulations! It's fantastic that you secured that volunteer role.

Thanks! It's great. Can you suggest some really comfortable steel-toed boots? The concrete floors at the museum are brutal on my feet after a few hours, and my old work boots are completely worn through the soles. I need something that actually has some arch support for once.
Timberland PRO and Red Wing are both highly recommended for long hours on concrete floors, offering great support and durability.

I'll check out Red Wing, there's a store near my house. Also, the maritime museum wants me to join their board of directors next year because of my expertise. Wild, right? Me, a grease monkey, sitting on a board of directors making decisions about museum exhibits and funding.
That is a tremendous honor! Being asked to join the board of directors speaks volumes about how much they value your expertise.

Are Red Wings true to size? Because my feet are kinda wide, and the last time I ordered boots online they pinched my toes so bad I couldn't walk for a week. If I'm going to spend the money, I want to make sure they actually fit right.
Red Wing boots typically run a bit large, so many people recommend sizing down by half a size for the best fit.

I am planning a trip to visit my friend Dave in Florida this winter. He's been bragging about the weather down there. What's the cheapest way to ship my tools down there? I want to help him fix up a boat he bought, but I refuse to fly with heavy wrenches.
For heavy tools, less-than-truckload (LTL) freight carriers or services like UShip, where independent drivers bid on your load, are usually the most cost-effective options.

UShip looks like a pretty good option, I'll look into it. My physical therapy appointment changed to Wednesdays at 9 AM. The therapist had a baby so her whole schedule shifted around, which means I have to rearrange my mornings now, but it's fine. I'm just glad to keep seeing her.
Got it. Adjusting your routine for a Wednesday morning appointment might take a week or two to get used to.

Also, big news, I officially obtained dual US and Canadian citizenship! The paperwork came through last month after what felt like years of waiting and sending in birth certificates. So now I can hop the border whenever I want without feeling like I'm being interrogated at the crossing.
Congratulations on officially getting your dual citizenship! That's wonderful news after waiting for the paperwork.

How much does UShip usually cost for a 50lb crate of dense metal tools? I don't want to get scammed by some astronomical shipping rate when the tools themselves are only worth a few hundred bucks. If it's too much, I might just drive down there instead of flying.
Shipping a 50lb crate cross-country on UShip typically ranges from $100 to $250, depending on the route and driver availability.

Got it, I'll check their website and see if I can get a quote. If it's under two hundred bucks I'll probably just ship it and save myself the headache of a multi-day drive. Thanks for the help sorting all this out, I really appreciate it.
Sounds like a plan. Safe travels when you head down to Florida!

Winter in Minneapolis is absolutely brutal right now. We had a deep freeze over the weekend and the biodiesel in my F-250 completely gelled up. I was stuck in my driveway for two hours with a heat gun trying to get the fuel lines to thaw out enough to start.
That is extremely frustrating. Biodiesel is notorious for gelling in severe cold unless you use heavy winter additives.

I'm totally done with it. I sold my diesel F-250 yesterday and I bought a used electric Ford Lightning. No more fuel issues, no more gelling, no more smelling like exhaust. It's a massive change for a mechanic to go electric, but I am just tired of the cold weather maintenance.
That's a major change! An electric truck like the Lightning will certainly solve the fuel gelling problems.

Yep, it's a completely different world. My cat Socks likes to sleep on the hood of my truck while it charges. She's a weird cat, but I guess the charging equipment puts off a little bit of heat, and since the truck is plugged in the garage, it's her new favorite spot.
Cats love warm spots, and the charging components probably give off just enough heat to make the hood perfectly cozy for Socks.

Does the severe cold affect the Lightning's battery range much? I know standard car batteries hate the cold, but I don't know how these massive lithium packs handle being parked in a freezing garage overnight. I don't want to be stranded on the highway on my way to a job.
Yes, extreme cold can reduce EV battery range by 20% to 40%, so you'll definitely want to keep it plugged in when parked during winter.

I think I'm done with the heavy stuff. I am semi-retiring to only do light diagnostic gig work. The heavy lifting is over. My back just can't take leaning over engine bays and pulling transmissions anymore. It's time to let the younger guys destroy their joints while I use my brain.
That is a huge life event! Congratulations on taking a step back to focus on the lighter, diagnostic side of your trade.

Yeah, it's a relief honestly. I need to update my resume just in case I want to apply for some consulting gigs though. Can you give me a template that makes me look professional? I haven't written a resume in twenty years, I've just been relying on word of mouth.
Here is a simple chronological template you can use to highlight your diagnostic experience.

Thanks, that template looks solid. The museum actually made me Head of Restoration on the board, so I am no longer doing hands-on engine restoring at the maritime museum. I am the Head of Restoration on the board of the maritime museum. I just run the meetings and direct the younger volunteers now.
That is wonderful! Transitioning to a leadership role on the board is a perfect fit for this new, semi-retired chapter.

Can you make the resume template emphasize consulting and project management over physical labor? I want anyone reading it to know that they are hiring me for my expertise and my ability to diagnose complex issues, not to turn a wrench for ten hours a day in the hot sun.
I have adjusted the template to focus on consulting, diagnostics, and project management rather than physical repairs.

My laptop screen keeps flickering when I open it past 90 degrees. It's driving me absolutely crazy. If I keep it half closed it's fine, but the second I push it back to a normal viewing angle, the whole screen just starts strobing and flashing colors. What could be causing that?
That sounds like a loose or damaged display cable passing through the laptop's hinge.

Yeah, probably the cable. I'll open it up. My friend Steve is helping me organize my single garage unit later today. The wall between garage units 4A and 4B is back up, so it's incredibly cramped in there now. We have to figure out how to stack everything vertically.
Good luck with the organization. It takes some clever storage solutions to make a single garage unit feel spacious again.

Thanks. Oh, and I bought three bottles of 10mg Lisinopril by mistake instead of my 40mg script. My brain is completely fried. I was just clicking through the online pharmacy portal trying to get it done fast, and I didn't even check the dosage before hitting the confirm button.
Mistakes happen. You should call your pharmacy to see if they can exchange them for the correct dosage.

Nah, my doctor lowered my Lisinopril dose to 20mg anyway since my BP is down. I guess not smelling like biodiesel exhaust and actually getting off my feet a bit helped. I'll just take two 10s for the next month instead of paying for a new 20mg prescription. Problem solved. Plus with Steve helping me reorganize the shop, I won't be tripping over jacks anymore.
I am so glad to hear your health is improving and your dose was lowered! Using up the 10mg bottles is a practical solution.

Are display cables universal or model-specific? Like, can I just buy a generic ribbon cable off the internet, or do I need to hunt down the exact part number for this specific laptop model? I really don't want to wait three weeks for a part to ship from overseas.
Display cables are highly model-specific, so you will need to order one made exactly for your laptop's make and model.

Okay, I understand the process now. I'll book an appointment with the local town hall first thing tomorrow morning so we can get this paperwork moving as quickly as possible.
That is the best way to handle it. Let me know if you need help with any other visa documents.

I need you to draft a cover letter for me. I applied for a Head Brewer position at Basqueland Brewing in March 2025. I've been at my current place for five years and I think it's time for a step up. Emphasise my 5 years at my current small village brewery. Make it sound like leaving my manager at my current brewery, Gorka, is an incredibly tough choice, not a desperate flee from a sinking ship. Keep it professional but add a bit of personality.
Here is a draft cover letter highlighting your five years of experience. It frames your desire to move on as seeking new challenges and growth opportunities.

That is absolutely perfect. I am aiming for a salary of 50,000 euros, hopefully this letter is strong enough to get me an interview. In my spare time, I have started a woodworking hobby. I am making birdhouses, maybe we can weave that in as a fun personal detail?
Birdhouse making is a great detail! It shows craftsmanship and patience. I can weave that into the final paragraph as a personal touch.

Good idea, I like how you integrated that. Side note: I brew with liquid yeast on Tuesdays right now. Can you explicitly mention I'm very familiar with that specific schedule and yeast management? It's a huge part of the job I'm applying for.
I have updated the letter to highlight your expertise with liquid Wyeast and the Tuesday brewing cycle. It demonstrates you can hit the ground running.

Thanks, the draft looks really solid and professional now. If I actually get the job and the salary bump, I am considering buying a boat. But I shouldn't get ahead of myself before the interview even happens.
A head brewer salary and a boat sounds like an excellent combination!
Can we make the second paragraph a bit punchier? It feels a bit passive. And should I include my references directly on the letter, or leave them off for now to save space?
Here is a punchier version using stronger action verbs. Just write "References available upon request" at the bottom instead of listing them.
Understood, that makes a lot of sense. I will just write 'References available upon request' and finally send this application off. Thanks for your help.
You are very welcome. Best of luck with the application!

I need a layout plan for a 4x4 raised bed vegetable garden for my backyard. Please make the instructions completely idiot-proof, because my track record with keeping plants alive isn't exactly stellar.
Here is a simple layout for a 4x4 raised bed: tomatoes and peppers in the back, bush beans in the middle, and carrots and radishes in the front.

Nice, that sounds manageable. In other news, I work as a head brewer at Basqueland Brewing under my new manager Eneko! But the commute is long, and my manager Eneko wears a lot of Patagonia, which is an entirely new corporate vibe for me to get used to.
Congratulations on getting the Head Brewer position! That is fantastic news, even with the new commute.

Thanks! Because of the long commute, I have dropped my woodworking hobby completely. I just have absolutely no time to make anything anymore. So right now, I just want to focus on this garden and see if I can successfully grow some tomatoes this summer.
Understood. Let's stick to just tomatoes then—they are very rewarding and require less daily maintenance than a full vegetable patch.

That is very helpful advice. Also, as a major update at work, I brew with dry yeast on Thursdays now. Switching away from liquid yeast completely shifted my schedule and my entire life rhythm feels ruined. I'm hoping the gardening will give me some peace and quiet.
Switching from liquid to dry yeast and changing brew days is a huge adjustment. You will eventually find a new rhythm!

I will definitely need that peace. Can you list the exact soil composition I should buy from the garden center for the tomatoes, and do they need full sun all day or is partial shade fine in the afternoons?
I recommend 50% topsoil, 30% compost, and 20% perlite. Yes, they need full sun, at least 6-8 hours of direct light daily.
Great, that spot right next to the shed will work perfectly then, it gets blasted with sunlight all morning. I'll go buy the soil bags this weekend and get started.
Excellent. Make sure the shed doesn't block the morning sun, and they should do wonderfully. Happy gardening!

I desperately need a new workout plan that doesn't involve using my left knee at all. Unfortunately, I tore my left meniscus playing rugby in late July 2025, and I am currently hobbling around feeling incredibly sorry for myself and going a bit stir-crazy.
Here is a seated upper body and core workout plan you can do: seated dumbbell presses, seated rows, core twists, and seated bicep curls.

Thanks for the suggestions. My surgeon was very blunt with me at the consultation: I can no longer play rugby, ever again. The joint just won't handle the impact. I am now officially a fragile antique and I have to find a new way to stay active.
I am so sorry to hear that. Being told you have to give up a sport you love is really tough news to process.

Yeah, it really sucks to lose that part of my life. Also, my Aloña Mendi mountain climbing club membership lapsed in 2025 because, as you might guess, mountains require functional knees. I guess I'll just have to get really exceptionally good at seated bench pressing instead of climbing.
Bench pressing is a great alternative! Let's adapt your program to focus heavily on upper body strength while keeping your knee completely safe.
I turned 36 years old in July 2025, so I suppose it's about time my body started aggressively rejecting high-impact sports. It just happened a bit more suddenly than I was mentally prepared for.
Happy belated birthday! 36 is a great age, even if the joints are starting to complain a little louder.

Thanks, I appreciate the optimism. Can you put those upper body exercises into a clean weekly table format? Also, could you swap the pull-ups for something using dumbbells, since I don't have a pull-up bar installed at home yet?
Here is the weekly table format, with all lower-body stress removed. I have swapped the pull-ups for seated dumbbell rows as requested.
Perfect, those seated rows will do nicely. I'll start the new routine on Monday and just focus on building my upper body strength while the knee slowly heals.
Take it slow and focus on form to avoid injuring anything else!

I really need you to help me reorganize my monthly budget spreadsheet, because things are looking pretty grim financially. My father-in-law Koldo passed away in September 2025, and dealing with the aftermath has been incredibly stressful on multiple fronts.
I am so sorry for your loss. Here is a budgeting framework that can help you clearly see your new monthly obligations and find areas to adjust.

Thanks. The house feels completely different and very quiet now. My mother-in-law Begoña has arthritis and she is really struggling with her mobility and the grief at the same time. It has been an exceptionally tough couple of weeks for everyone living here.
It sounds like an incredibly difficult time for your whole family. It is completely normal for everyone to be struggling right now.

On top of all the funeral costs that we're dealing with, which are astronomical, I send 300 euros to my mother in Colombia every month now to help her out. The financial stress is piling up. Also, someone at work told me I need to eat less cheese for my health, but I'm completely ignoring that advice because cheese is my only comfort right now. Can we look at where I can realistically cut costs?
I have updated the spreadsheet to reflect the 300 euros for your mother. I have completely ignored the cheese advice, as requested.

That updated spreadsheet helps clear things up, thank you. Can you also add a row for emergency savings and include a formula to automatically calculate exactly 10% of my net income so I don't have to do the math manually?
I have added an emergency savings row. The formula `=B2*0.10` will calculate 10% of your net income automatically.
That formula works perfectly. One more question, how should I categorize the annual property tax in a monthly budget spreadsheet so it doesn't totally blindside us when the bill arrives?
Property tax is best handled by taking the annual amount, dividing it by 12, and putting it under a 'Housing Expenses' category.
Okay, I'll divide the total annual amount by 12 and put it under the housing expenses category. That way the money is just sitting there ready when the time comes.
That will make sure you are slowly setting aside the money for it all year round.

I need some Christmas gift ideas, and I am completely stuck. My daughter Lucia is 11 years old, but she acts like she's 25. My daughter Lucia wants skincare products for Christmas in 2025, but I really want her to want something age-appropriate like Legos.
For an 11-year-old interested in skincare, gentle brands like CeraVe or Bubble have fun packaging but are safe for young skin. A Lego Botanicals set could be a good compromise too!

An 'age-appropriate moisturiser' might be the depressing compromise I need to make to keep the peace. On another note, I am taking 10mg of Rizatriptan for my migraines now. The doctor finally gave up on the old medication and decided we needed to try a totally different class of drugs.
It's good that Dr. Arana is trying a new approach. Rizatriptan works differently than Sumatriptan, so hopefully, it provides better relief.

Yeah, let's hope so. Because if this new medication doesn't work, I joked about considering amateur trepanation for my migraines, just to release the pressure. I'm kidding, mostly, but the pain really does make you consider some very drastic, medieval solutions.
I strongly advise against amateur surgery! Let's hope the 10mg Rizatriptan does the trick instead.

I promise I'll leave the power tools in the shed. Could you suggest a few specific brands for the moisturiser that don't have harsh chemical actives that would ruin an eleven-year-old's perfectly fine skin?
CeraVe's Hydrating Facial Cleanser and their daily moisturizing lotion are very safe, fragrance-free options without harsh actives.
CeraVe looks like a very reasonable, boring, and safe option, which is exactly what I'm looking for. Do you know if I can easily buy that at a normal pharmacy or a standard grocery store?
Yes, CeraVe is widely available at most standard pharmacies and supermarkets.
Great, I'll grab a bottle of it on my way home from the brewery this evening. Thanks for helping me navigate the terrifying world of tweens.
You're welcome! I hope Lucia likes it.

I need you to draft a formal email to the local council asking about permits for building a shed in the garden. It needs to be extremely polite but firm, sort of like the tone of a disappointed headmaster who expects better communication.
Here is a draft email to the council. It firmly asks for clarification on shed permits and requests a timeline, keeping a professional but expectant tone.

That is a perfect draft. Fun fact about the shed: my family's heirloom grandfather clock is in the shed now. We had to move it out of the hallway because the chiming was a precise trigger for my migraines. It's now serenading the lawnmower instead of us.
That is quite the solution! I'm glad the clock is out of the house if the chiming was triggering your migraines.

The email draft is fine exactly as it is, I won't change a word. In more positive news, I have resumed my woodworking hobby! I am making small boxes while sitting down at a workbench, which is a great way to enjoy it without putting any strain on my injured knee.
That is great news! Making small boxes is a wonderful way to enjoy woodworking without putting any strain on your knee.

It really is great for my mental health to be building things again. Could you actually reword the last paragraph of the council email to be slightly more polite? It feels a tiny bit too aggressive upon second read.
I have softened the final paragraph to read: 'I would be grateful if you could clarify the timeline for this process at your earliest convenience.'
Yes, that softened version is much better, thank you. What is the usual response time for these kinds of minor structural council queries? Should I expect to wait weeks or months?
Council queries regarding minor structures typically take between 10 to 14 working days for an initial response.
Okay, I'll set a reminder to follow up if I don't hear back in two weeks then. Thanks again for drafting that, dealing with local bureaucracy always gives me a headache.
That is a realistic expectation. Let me know if you need help following up if they are late.

I urgently need a recipe for a Sunday lunch that looks incredibly impressive to guests but requires absolutely zero culinary skill or active attention from me. I'll be feeding 6 hungry adults and I don't want to spend the entire afternoon stressing out in the kitchen.
A slow-roasted shoulder of lamb or pork is perfect. You just season it, put it in the oven on low for hours, and it does all the work itself.

That slow-roasted pork shoulder looks totally doable and delicious. By the way, my doctor, Dr. Arana, retired before April 2026, which is super annoying. I am seeing Dr. Etxebarria for my migraines now, and having to explain my entire medical history to someone new was exhausting.
It can be frustrating to change doctors, but hopefully Dr. Etxebarria brings a fresh perspective to managing your migraines.

Yeah, she seems competent though. She listened to me and then immediately took action. I am taking 15mg of Rizatriptan for my migraines now, which is a pretty hefty bump. I feel like I am now mostly composed of various pharmaceuticals rather than actual human cells.
15mg is a strong dose, but if it finally gets the migraines under control, it is definitely worth it.

Let's hope this higher dose finally does the trick, because I'm running out of options. Back to the lunch recipe: how long exactly does the pork roast need to stay in the oven per kilo to get that fall-apart texture?
For a slow-roasted pork shoulder, you want about 45 minutes per kilo at 160°C (320°F), plus an extra 30 minutes at the end.
Got it, 45 minutes per kilo sounds easy enough to calculate. Should I make sure to cover the roasting tin tightly in aluminum foil for the first half of the cooking time to stop it drying out?
Yes, cover it tightly with foil for the first two-thirds of the cooking time, then remove it so the outside can crisp up.
That makes complete sense, I definitely don't want the outside to burn before the inside is fully tender. I'll write down those exact timings so I don't ruin Sunday lunch.
Exactly. It will be incredibly tender on the inside and crispy on the outside.

I need a quick technology comparison. Can you compare the MacBook Air M3 and the Dell XPS 13 for me? It needs to smoothly handle my incredibly huge, complicated spreadsheets and also survive the fact that my mother-in-law keeps 400 browser tabs open simultaneously at all times.
The MacBook Air M3 is excellent for battery life and handles heavy spreadsheets silently. The Dell XPS 13 is also very capable but might run a bit warmer with 400 tabs open.

The Mac might actually be better for her chaotic tab situation then, thanks. Just FYI, inflation is hitting us really hard lately, and I send 400 euros to my mother Carmen every month now to make sure she's comfortable, so I'm trying to make a smart, long-lasting investment with this laptop purchase.
Inflation is hitting everyone hard. Sending 400 euros is a very generous commitment to your mother.

Yeah, it's a significant chunk of change, but it's necessary. Also, in fantastic news, the brewery management finally had a moment of clarity and reversed their decision. I brew with liquid yeast on Tuesdays again! Nature is healing and my schedule is finally back to a rhythm that actually makes sense.
That is great news! Liquid yeast and a Tuesday schedule sound like things are finally back to normal at the brewery.
It really is a massive relief to be back to my old routine. Regarding the laptops, what is the exact battery life difference between the two models under normal, non-intensive working conditions?
The MacBook Air M3 typically gets around 14-16 hours of real-world battery life, while the Dell XPS 13 usually averages 10-12 hours depending on the display.
That's a pretty clear win for the Mac then. Does the Dell XPS 13 happen to come with a touch screen option, or are they both strictly traditional clamshell displays?
Yes, the Dell XPS 13 does have a touch screen option, whereas the MacBook Air does not.

Having a touch screen is nice, but I think I'll ultimately go with the Mac. It just seems much simpler and more reliable for the entire family to use without me having to provide constant tech support.
The Mac is definitely known for its longevity and ease of use. It should handle the family's needs perfectly.

turns.text: Text too small on screen 👓. Need bigger font on my iPhone SE second gen. Hard to read bus schedules. Retired from driving tour buses 3 years ago but eyes still tired from decades of highway glare 🚌.
Go to Settings > Accessibility > Display & Text Size, then tap Larger Text and drag the slider to the right. You can also turn on Bold Text right above it to make the letters easier to distinguish.
Done 👍. Much clearer now.
Glad to hear that. You can also toggle Button Shapes on that same screen if you want outline borders around interactive icons.
Button shapes help too 🔘. But menus still feel cramped. Can I make the home screen app icons bigger as well?
On your model, you can go to Settings > Display & Brightness > Display Zoom and select 'Larger Text' to scale up app icons and interface elements across the whole system.

Icons look great now 📱. Next problem: monthly budget reminders. Living alone in Jalatlaco, have to send 1,400 pesos every month for my old UnADM distance degree loan 💸. High blood pressure meds already take 50 mg losartan daily 💊. Need simple reminder system.

You can set a repeating monthly reminder in the built-in Reminders app titled 'UnADM Loan Payment' with an alarm date. For expenses, keeping a pinned checklist note in Apple Notes makes tracking easy without downloading extra apps.
Apple Notes works 📝. Writing my medical note too. Penicillins give me bad hives 🚫, need clinic warning handy. Old email ramiro_tours_oax@yahoo.com still gets the tuition statements ✉️.
You can create a note titled 'Emergency Medical Info' with your allergy and losartan dose, then swipe right on the note in your list and tap the pin icon to keep it at the top.

Cardiologist yelled at me on Monday 🫀. Blood pressure still stubborn. Doctor bumped my daily losartan to 100 mg last Tuesday. Need a low-impact walking plan. I am 79 years old, knees creak on cobblestones 🦿.

Start with 15 to 20 minutes of steady walking on flat ground, followed by five minutes of seated ankle circles and gentle calf stretches. Walk at a conversational pace four days a week, and pause if you notice any joint pain or lightheadedness.
Flat ground is fine 🚶‍♂️. Walked 45 minutes every morning in El Llano park during early November 2024 🌳.
That is strong endurance, but keep an eye on your knees after 45 minutes on hard pavement. Splitting that into two 20-minute sessions morning and evening can protect your cartilage.
What stretches help knees before walking? Stiff in mornings.
Before walking, do gentle standing hamstring curls by lifting your heel toward your buttocks, along with seated knee extensions. Keep movements smooth and avoid bouncing.

Good routine 🧎‍♂️. Afternoon rest is sacred though. Drink cinnamon-infused hibiscus tea every afternoon at 4:00 PM ☕. Also busy organizing our barrio chapel festival, serving as head mayordomo for San Matías Jalatlaco this year ⛪. Lots of standing.

That festival stewardship is a meaningful honor, but festival standing is hard on the back and joints. Wear supportive cushioned shoes with arch support during committee duties and drink plenty of water.
Will wear sneakers under the trousers 👍. Thanks.
Cushioned sneakers will make a huge difference. Enjoy the festival preparations and your afternoon tea.
Learning Valley Zapotec 🗣️. Want to surprise Beatriz. She is an artisan weaver from Teotitlán del Valle, we started dating two months ago ❤️. Need basic polite morning greetings.

In Central Valley Zapotec, a standard respectful morning greeting is 'Padxiux' (or 'Padiush'), derived from 'God give you good day'. Another warm phrase is 'Sicarú siado'', meaning 'beautiful morning'.
Practicing aloud 🗣️. Taking Zapotec language classes on Tuesday evenings at Instituto Cultural Oaxaca 📚.
Repetition with a native speaker like Beatriz will make those sounds natural quickly. Writing phonetic notes in your class notebook will reinforce the tones.
How do I say 'thank you very much' in Valley Zapotec?
You can say 'Xquixe pe' lii' to one person, or simply 'Xquixhe' for 'thanks'.

Noted down ✍️. Told my sister Teresa in Tehuacán about Beatriz, she teased me 👵. Also dealing with property paperwork 📑. Agreed to sell my half-share of inherited house in Barrio de Xochimilco to a local ceramicist. Buyer deposited earnest money in escrow last Friday 🏠.
Having escrow confirmed is a reassuring step in Mexican real estate transactions. Be sure your notary public reviews the chain of title and predial property tax receipts before scheduling signing.
Notary has all tax receipts 📂. Fingers crossed.
Sounds like you have your paperwork in order. Best of luck with the closing and with your language studies.

Mechanic estimate arrived 🚗. My 2008 Nissan Tsuru with 320,000 kilometers broke down on camino a Tlacolula last weekend. Cracked transmission casing and stripped clutch. Workshop wants 18,500 pesos for rebuilt gearbox and labor. Is that excessive 🔧?

For a 2008 Tsuru with that mileage, 18,500 pesos is roughly 35 to 40 percent of the car's entire resale value. Unless the chassis and engine are in pristine condition, investing that much into a major transmission swap often leads to diminishing returns.
What would a junkyard pay for parts?
A local deshuesadero or scrapyard typically pays between 3,500 and 6,000 pesos for an intact rolling Tsuru shell with a salvageable engine block.

Might let it sit in yard for now 🤷‍♂️. Rough week overall. The sale of my Xochimilco house fell through completely! Buyer mortgage denied, contract canceled, escrow deposit refunded yesterday ❌. Back to square one with that property.
That is very discouraging news after having escrow open, but failed bank approvals happen frequently. Holding onto the deed leaves your options open to find a cash buyer or rent the space.
True. Oh, quick correction on my Zapotec classes 📝! I said Tuesdays earlier — checked my fee receipt, it is actually Thursday evenings at Instituto Cultural Oaxaca 🗓️.
Understood, I have updated the schedule note to Thursday evenings.
Thanks 👍. Will sleep on the car decision.
Taking a couple of days before deciding on the car is a wise move. Have a restful evening.

Looking for books on colonial Mexican medicinal plants 🌿. Started a 6-month certification course in botanical docent studies at Centro de las Artes de San Agustín (CASA) 🏛️. Classes on weekends. Need solid introductory texts.

A cornerstone text is the *Libellus de Medicinalibus Indorum Herbis* (the Badianus Codex), compiled in 1552 with indigenous botanical illustrations. Another essential source is Francisco Hernández's *Historia Natural de Nueva España*, commissioned by the Spanish crown to document Mesoamerican flora.
Will look for Spanish facsimile editions 📖. Are they available in public archives?
Yes, UNAM produced high-quality facsimile editions with modern Spanish translations and botanical indices, which specialized regional libraries usually hold.

Can check at Biblioteca Henestrosa, have an active library card there 🪪. Friend Don Silvio recommended John Hilton's memoirs too 🌵. Also, finally dumped my Yahoo mail ✉️. Hacked again. Switched my primary email address to ramiro.oaxaca@proton.me last week 🔒.
Proton is a far safer choice with its built-in encryption. Make sure to update your contact email with your banking institutions, UnADM, and the CASA administration.
Updated bank and utility accounts already 👍.
Great job handling those security updates. Enjoy your research at Biblioteca Henestrosa.

Can you translate short German excerpt from an old tourist insurance archival letter? 'Hiermit bestätigen wir den Eingang der Unterlagen bezüglich des Vorfalls...' 🚌. Drove tour buses across Oaxaca for 35 years before retiring, but back in the 1960s I drove freight trucks through the Sierra Norte 🚛. Found this in an old tin box.
It translates to: 'We hereby confirm receipt of the documents regarding the incident...' It is a standard bureaucratic acknowledgment confirming they received submitted paperwork.
Just an old claim acknowledgment from 1998 then 🗑️. Good to know.
Exactly, it holds no outstanding obligations or actions required.

Got a stressful municipal notice from Panteón General 🪦. My late brother Hector has been in a five-year temporary ground grave there since 2020. Lease expiring. City says we must exhume remains and transfer to a wall ossuary niche by December 💀. Heavy paperwork.

Municipal cemetery regulations typically mandate exhumation upon lease expiration to clear ground plots. You will need your brother's original death certificate and family identification documents for the municipal health and cemetery offices.

Have his papers 📁. But worried about mama Consuelo. She is 101, living at Hogar San José in Puebla 👵. Admitted to hospital infirmary two days ago with respiratory congestion 🏥. Heading up on night bus to Puebla.
Traveling to be at her side is the most important thing. I hope the medical team resolves her respiratory congestion quickly, and please take care of yourself during the bus journey.
Packed my overnight bag 🧳. Thanks for the help.
Safe travels to Puebla. Wishing your mother a steady recovery.

Finished docent course at CASA! Starting part-time work as weekend docent at Jardín Etnobotánico de Oaxaca 🌱. 10 hours a week, no longer fully retired 🏛️. Need help drafting short email to coordinator confirming uniform size medium.

You can write: 'Estimada Coordinadora, le confirmo con gusto que mi talla de camisa para el uniforme es mediana. Quedo atento a las indicaciones para iniciar mis guardias de fin de semana en el Jardín. Saludos cordiales, Ramiro.'
Sent to coordinator 👍. Fits well.
That will ensure your onboarding kit is ready for your first shift.

Big news at home 🏡. Beatriz moved into my house in Barrio de Jalatlaco last week! No longer living alone ❤️. We adopted a stray three-legged cat from the alley, named him Chapulín 🐈. Also had to finance a rooftop solar water heater ☀️. Took out a 28,000 peso loan from Caja Popular Mexicana 🏦.
Congratulations on moving in together and giving Chapulín a loving home! A solar water heater will drastically lower your LP gas cylinder expenses, making the monthly credit payments very manageable.
Gas bill should drop by half 🔥. Worth the investment.
With Oaxaca's sunshine, you should see hot water savings immediately. Enjoy settling into your new routine together.
Sad news 🕯️. My mother Consuelo passed away peacefully last week at Hogar San José in Puebla at age 101 🕊️. Need help drafting formal family bereavement note for our relatives.

Here is a heartfelt notice: 'Con profunda tristeza participamos el sensible fallecimiento de nuestra amada madre, Doña Consuelo, ocurrido en Puebla a los 101 años de edad. Agradecemos sus oraciones por su eterno descanso y su solidario acompañamiento en este doloroso momento.'
Sent to family group 📱. Thank you.
My sincere condolences to you and your family. Reaching 101 is a remarkable life, and I hope her memory brings warmth amidst the grief.

Heavy month. While in Puebla and Oaxaca settling estates, finally completed cemetery transfer for my brother Hector 🪦. Exhumation done, transferred his remains into a perpetual wall niche at Panteón General 🏛️. Cousin Jorge in Veracruz bought a new motorcycle, rode to funeral 🏍️. Sister Teresa couldn't stay in Tehuacán after mama died, so she moved to Orizaba, Veracruz, to live near her daughter 📦.

Resolving your brother's perpetual niche brings closure to an important family duty, and having Teresa close to her daughter will give her great comfort. Be gentle with yourself after such a demanding period.
Resting quietly today 🫖. Beatriz making atole.
Rest and quiet family comfort are what you need most right now. Take care.

iPhone SE battery puffed up like a taco last month, totally dead 📵. Bought a refurbished Samsung Galaxy A34 📱. Need help installing and configuring Libby for library audiobooks. Android menus confuse me.

Open Google Play Store, search for 'Libby', and tap Install. Once open, follow the prompt asking if you have a library card, search for your institution, and enter your card credentials to start browsing.
Installed and card linked 🎧! Testing an audiobook now.
You can tap the dial icon in the player to adjust narration speed or set a sleep timer if you listen before bed.

Audiobooks will help rest 🩺. Cardiologist visit yesterday. Blood pressure dipped too low on 100 mg losartan, getting dizzy spells standing up. Doctor reduced my losartan back to 50 mg daily 💊. Also stepped down as head mayordomo for San Matías Jalatlaco festival ⛪. Doctor said no more festival crowds and stress.

Stepping down from demanding civic leadership to protect your health is a wise decision. Reducing losartan back to 50 mg should clear up the dizziness, but be sure to stand up gradually and stay hydrated.
Already feeling less dizzy today 👍.
That is very good news. Enjoy your audiobooks and take things at a calm pace.

Need to write formal message to cadastral surveyor 📐. Surveyor measured boundary stakes of our Xochimilco family lot wrong by two meters along north wall. Need him to recheck boundary markers against registered title 📜.

You can send: 'Estimado Ingeniero, revisando el plano topográfico preliminar del predio en Barrio de Xochimilco, identifiqué una discrepancia de dos metros en el lindero norte respecto al título de propiedad. Le solicito cordialmente una revisión en campo para rectificar las mojoneras perimetrales.'
Copied and sent to his office 📨.
Having that formal written request on record ensures the boundary adjustment is officially documented before any new deeds are drafted.

Very sad month here 💔. Beatriz and I broke up two weeks ago. Too many disagreements about the future. She moved out of my house and went back to Teotitlán del Valle 🧶. Living alone again in Jalatlaco with cat Chapulín 🐈.
I am truly sorry to hear that. Breakups are deeply painful, especially after sharing a home. Allow yourself space to grieve the relationship, and lean on Chapulín's steady companionship.
Chapulín keeps me grounded 🐾. Thinking of planning a quiet visit to the graphic arts workshop in San Agustín Etla in autumn 2026 🍁. Need creative inspiration.
Visiting the paper and printmaking studios at CASA Etla in autumn will be wonderfully soothing and restorative.

How to translate phrase: '¿Bi láatzi' lii?' 🗣️. Stopped attending group Zapotec classes at Instituto Cultural Oaxaca last month. Classroom too noisy for my ears. Switched to private weekly tutoring at home with Maestro Fausto 👨‍🏫.
In Valley Zapotec, '¿Bi láatzi' lii?' translates literally to 'What does your heart desire?' and is used idiomatically to ask 'What would you like?' or 'How can I help you?'.
Very poetic phrase ❤️. Maestro Fausto is great.
One-on-one tutoring allows you to explore cultural idioms like that at your own speed without classroom distraction.

Finally cleared the back patio 🚗! Sold my broken 2008 Nissan Tsuru to a scrapyard for scrap metal. Flatbed hauled it away Friday, got 4,500 pesos 💵. Now I collect vintage hand-carved wooden alebrijes from San Martín Tilcajete to display on the patio shelves 🦎.
Parting with the broken car frees up physical space and mental energy. Showcasing Tilcajete alebrijes on open shelves will bring wonderful artisan color to your patio.
Patio looks lively now 🪵. Wooden jaguar looks fierce!
Tilcajete copal carvings are true treasures. Enjoy your quiet patio study space.
Summer heat getting intense in Oaxaca ☀️. Need a shaded morning walking route near Jalatlaco for my 30-minute daily walk 🚶‍♂️. Too much sun on Niños Héroes avenue.

Try walking north along Calle Curtidurías into Barrio de Xochimilco, following the colonial stone aqueduct of San Felipe. The tall trees along the arches cast deep morning shade and vehicle traffic is very light.
Love the stone aqueduct 🧱. Perfect shade.
The stone arches also keep the air slightly cooler in the morning, making it gentle on your heart and joints.
Celebrate with me 🎉! Made my final payment to UnADM yesterday! Student loan debt from my distance degree is 100% paid off 🎓💸. Free of that 1,400 peso monthly installment after all these years!
That is a wonderful achievement, Ramiro! Paying off your university debt in full brings real financial peace of mind. You should be very proud of completing both your degree and the payments.
Huge weight lifted 😌. Still paying monthly loan installments to Caja Popular Mexicana for the solar water heater ☀️, but having only one loan makes my pension stretch much further!
Having just the solar heater payment makes budgeting much simpler. Enjoy your debt-free milestone and your cool morning walks by the aqueduct.
